rounds.restatement: Add a {{RAW}}...{{END_RAW}} block to the template resolver, done only in the lexer: after a tag whose trimmed content is exactly RAW, everything up to the first END_RAW tag becomes one ordinary Text token (not trimmed, CRLF turned into LF, no token when empty). The parser and interpreter stay untouched, so the block repeats in loops and vanishes in untaken branches like any other text. An unclosed RAW must throw the lexer's SyntaxError at the RAW tag's line and column, templates without RAW must behave exactly as before, and the README must gain one RAW section with an accurate example. No nesting, escapes or options.

Separately, the project goal says 'correct for the n8n node', while the spec puts the n8n node file out of scope; if the node inspects the template text outside the lexer, the card cannot meet the cycle goal inside its own scope (see f1).

findings.title: Strict Mode / variable detection in the n8n node may still treat ${{name}} inside RAW as a required variable

serves.scenario: A prompt template holding a literal code sample such as {{RAW}}${{name}}{{END_RAW}} is run in the n8n node with Strict Mode on (the documented default) and no mapping for 'name'. If the node detects variables by scanning the template text rather than the lexer's tokens, it reports 'name' as missing and errors, so the template still cannot include tag-like text in the node. The detection code is not in the packet, so this is unverified.

findings.rubric: Goal-critical question 1 (everything between RAW and END_RAW comes out exactly as written); project goal 'correct for the n8n node'
findings.reproduction: In the n8n node, set Template to '{{RAW}}${{name}}{{END_RAW}}', leave Variable Mappings empty, keep Strict Mode on and enable Show Detected Variables. Expected: output '${{name}}', no error, and 'name' absent from detected_variables and missing_variables. Failure: a missing-variable error, or 'name' listed. If it fails, the smallest fix is to make detection ignore RAW spans, which needs a scope exception because the node file is out of scope.

findings.title: Render-level preservation of leading/trailing whitespace and blank lines in raw text is untested

serves.scenario: c3 says the raw text is not trimmed, but the only rb-03 test stops at the lexer. The raw content is emitted as an ordinary Text token, so any whitespace handling the unchanged parser or interpreter applies to text (trimming block bodies, dropping newlines next to block tags, collapsing blank lines) would also apply to raw content. A multi-line code sample inside an IF or FOR body could then lose its leading newline or indentation. The parser and interpreter are not in the packet, so this is unverified.

findings.title: Closing-tag match allows only spaces and tabs inside the braces

serves.scenario: The spec says the closing tag may have inner spaces 'as other tags do'. Other tags are matched on their trimmed content, which presumably also tolerates a newline inside the braces. The regex /\{\{[ \t]*END_RAW[ \t]*\}\}/ does not, so '{{RAW}}x{{END_RAW\n}}' is reported as an unclosed RAW block. This is a polish-level inconsistency and no criterion fails on it.
